ranked_facts.why: The presence of brownish macules on the hands and feet, hyperchromic punctate lesions on the trunk, and onychodystrophy is more characteristic of Cronkhite-Canada Syndrome, which is a subtype of B1, than of the other candidate branches.

The presence of numerous sessile and subpedunculated polyps throughout the colon and rectum is more characteristic of certain subtypes of B1, such as Familial Adenomatous Polyposis, Juvenile Polyposis Syndrome, and Cronkhite-Canada Syndrome, than of the other candidate branches.
